page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 6 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixed profile, largely influenced by the shared CPU allocation. The instance registers poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, falling into the bottom 10%, and weak multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25%. However, Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests position the server in the average tier for tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. Memory read bandwidth is average, though large-block write bandwidth and static web serving throughput are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU architecture and lack of local storage, this server offers a cost-effective resource density for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suited for general-purpose development environments, lightweight database operations, basic text processing, and moderate background tasks where resource sharing does not impact critical paths.
